DATA 201.title: Data in the Age of AI
DATA 201.description: Introduces major AI approaches and evaluates which questions they can answer, emphasizing data quality, generative-tool risks, transparent analysis and complementary model behavior.
DATA 201.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CSCI 140, 141, minimum score of 1 in 'CSCI 141 Equivalent', DATA 141, 101 or AAI 101. A minimum grade of D- is required in CSCI 140, CSCI 141, DATA 141, DATA 101 and AAI 101. Enrollment is limited to International Honours, Undergraduate or VCCS/RB Co-Enroll Articulation level students.
DATA 201.rationale: The actual description centers on AI approaches, modeling frameworks, appropriate strategy selection and failure modes, rather than generic programming or an inferred subject from the DATA prefix.

DATA 202.title: AI & Data Ethics
DATA 202.description: Examines ethical, legal, historical and social issues in data and AI, including privacy, discrimination, transparency, responsibility, research practice and system deployment.
DATA 202.prerequisites: Enrollment is limited to International Honours, Undergraduate or VCCS/RB Co-Enroll Articulation level students.
DATA 202.rationale: The full course description centers ethical and social analysis of AI/data systems; it does not become technical AI merely because AI is its object.

DATA 305.title: Designing AI Agents
DATA 305.description: Designs and evaluates agentic generative-AI workflows using prompt pipelines, retrieval augmentation, multi-agent methods and function-calling tools, with attention to reliability and ethical limits.
DATA 305.prerequisites: Prerequisite: DATA 201. A minimum grade of D- is required in DATA 201. Enrollment is limited to International Honours, Undergraduate or VCCS/RB Co-Enroll Articulation level students.
DATA 305.rationale: The actual description explicitly teaches construction and evaluation of generative-AI agent workflows and tools. Its technical AI subject is now supported by content, not the short title alone.
